analysis.title: The CEO Macro Briefing Book: Insights on the midterms
key_insights: Large and small caps both rallied on 4 November 2026 as election uncertainty cleared. The S&P 500 rose 1.58% to 7,688.62 and the Russell 2000 rose 1.58% to 2,856.95. UBS calls the move a broad rally predicated on lower oil prices.
WTI crude fell 8.29% to $88.12 on pressure to end the conflict with Iran. S&P 500 Energy fell 4.77% as lower oil hit producers.
Chip stocks sold off on expected scrutiny of data centers. SOX fell 3.13% to 10,268.65 while S&P 500 Tech rose 0.55%, with mega caps up and chips down.

Democrats campaigned on limiting AI. Democratic governors in Texas, Ohio and Georgia campaigned on restricting data-center development, and Texas holds about 27% of US data center capacity. House Democrats could establish a select committee on AI once seated.
As the odds of Democratic Senate control rose, so did credit spreads on hyperscalers. Companies with strong cloud capabilities rallied because existing cloud capacity would be more valuable.

UBS expects states may regulate to slow or stop data center construction, which could raise prices on existing cloud and compute capacity. Electricity costs are now political, and data centers may be pressed to pay a greater share of grid costs.

Gridlock is seen as more stable for long-term yields, but UBS says fiscal concerns matter more. The FY2026 deficit was USD 2.0te, or 6.2% of GDP, and reducing tariffs would lower revenue and add upward pressure on rates. UBS advises locking in fixed rates where possible rather than waiting for much lower long-term rates.

UBS argues Fed independence is better protected because every Fed board nominee needs Senate confirmation and Elizabeth Warren is expected to chair the committee that vets them. That lowers the odds of politically driven rate cuts but reduces upward pressure on long-end yields. UBS calls the outcome marginally more hawkish.
The 10Y Treasury yield fell 7.8 bps to 4.89% and the 2Y fell 4.8 bps to 4.59%. UBS attributes the 10Y move to lower oil and anticipated fiscal gridlock.
UBS says the odds the Fed holds rates in January are 71.00% (Kalshi), up from 79% per the table. The note says lower oil reduced pressure on the Fed to hike.
Credit spreads tightened: IG OAS fell 2 bp to 89 bp, IG Tech OAS fell 6 bp to 152 bp and HY OAS fell 11 bp to 324 bp.

S&P 500 Healthcare rose 3.05% as markets expect restoration of the ACA subsidies. House Democrats plan bills to restore the enhanced ACA subsidies, reverse Medicaid cuts and add legislative friction for the Iran war and tariffs.

M&A deal value is strong but concentrated in a few mega-deals by well-capitalized strategics, and deal counts remain soft. UBS sees a stable regulatory window over the next 12-24 months. Corporate buyers pay a median 11.6x EBITDA, above PE buyers, and tech, health care and government contracting deals should budget extra review time.

On tariffs, some existing tariffs need congressional extension after a Supreme Court ruling, which is unlikely under a Democratic majority. Congress can narrow the legal basis (Sections 232, 301 and 122), but tariffs under existing authority are unlikely to change wholesale.

Democrats can refuse a war supplemental and set funding limits in the defense bill, and the White House can veto. Subpoenas and hearings on the Iran war, AI, conflicts of interest and immigration enforcement may create headline risk without changing law or personnel.

sector_views.rationale: Healthcare rose 3.05% as markets expect restoration of ACA subsidies. UBS does not state a formal sector rating.
S&P 500 Energy fell 4.77% as lower oil hit producers amid Democratic scrutiny of the Iran conflict. UBS does not state a formal sector rating.
SOX fell 3.13% because data-center limits would threaten chip demand and the AI trade is rotating further.

Data-center restrictions could threaten chip demand and raise electricity costs.
Congressional hearings and subpoenas on the Iran war, AI, conflicts of interest and immigration enforcement create headline risk.
Democratic deals with the White House may add to the deficit or reduce tariff revenues.

tension_points.bear_case: Structural fiscal issues keep long yields elevated, with a 6.2% of GDP deficit, and reducing tariffs would cut revenue and widen the deficit.
